source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Increase compounding speed by allowing technique shortcuts whenever preparation volume is high in the pharmacy.","B":"Apply sterile-compounding controls only to oral products, because parenteral preparations do not require clean handling.","C":"Apply minimum sterile-compounding standards for facilities, personnel, processes, testing, and beyond-use controls.","D":"Replace environmental and personnel controls with final visual inspection, because sterility can be confirmed by sight."}}
source_row.rationale: USP <797> establishes personnel, environmental, process and quality controls for compounded sterile preparations to reduce contamination and other compounding-related patient risks; its purpose is safety, not workflow speed.
source_row.source_detail: USP <797> scope and purpose establish minimum standards for compounding sterile preparations to minimize harm including contamination, excessive endotoxins, variability and other quality failures. Official USP <797> chapter, current compounding standard including 2025 official text; rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: USP — General Chapter <797> Pharmaceutical Compounding—Sterile Preparations
source_row.stem: What is the primary patient-safety purpose of USP <797> requirements for compounded sterile preparations?
